impact.affected_asset: The /flag file placed in the challenge chroot.
impact.attacker_capability: A remote service client can submit a sequence of playbook, deletion, and run actions that drives the parser into an underflowed stack state and invokes the crafted execution path.
impact.security_effect: The supplied organizer exploit construction targets command execution that reads the challenge flag.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker can submit multiple playbook definitions and terminate a definition with an empty line while STEP nesting remains open.

The parser initializes a local stack pointer for each new playbook but accepts end-of-input without requiring balanced STEP/ENDSTEP state; a later parse can begin with ENDSTEP that has no matching STEP in that parse lifecycle.

On ENDSTEP, the parser decrements the stack pointer before checking whether nesting_depth is negative. A subsequent STEP dereferences the decremented pointer to store an allocated playbook identifier and indexes its parent as s.sp[-1].

The organizer solver uses the underflowed parser state with allocation/deletion layout shaping, then requests execution of playbook 601; its payload stages a note containing a flag-reading shell command, while the service healthcheck waits for a CTF flag marker.

failure.operation: Pre-decrement of the local parser stack pointer on unmatched ENDSTEP followed by STEP's dereference/indexing through that invalid pointer.

primary_invariant.kind: parser lifecycle and local stack bounds
primary_invariant.statement: Every ENDSTEP must match a STEP in the same new_playbook invocation, and s.sp must remain within the local stack array before decrement, dereference, or parent indexing.
primary_invariant.violated_because: An incomplete playbook is accepted at empty-line termination; a later invocation processes unmatched ENDSTEP and decrements s.sp before the negative-depth check, allowing the next STEP to write through an underflowed pointer.

quality.review_notes: Primary C source, organizer solution, solver, and deployed healthcheck are present. The healthcheck and solver define an intended remote flag oracle but do not themselves record a successful execution run. No upstream remediation patch is supplied; remediation is an invariant-based recommendation, not a claimed applied fix.

remediation.invariant_restored: Reject a playbook that terminates with open STEP nesting and reject ENDSTEP unless the local parser stack has a matching active STEP before decrementing or indexing s.sp.
mitigation_classes: balanced-grammar enforcement at end of input
stack-pointer bounds validation before pointer arithmetic and dereference

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The supplied solver creates many playbooks, deletes selected entries, submits an incomplete nested playbook, then starts another parse with ENDSTEP/STEP before requesting execution.
data_structure_invariants: s.sp must reference an element of s.stack before it is decremented, dereferenced, or used with s.sp[-1].
A completed playbook should have no unmatched open STEP state.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Defined as 10; the relevant invalid transition is a decrement below the stack base.
numeric_domains.name: MAX_NESTING_DEPTH

state_context.state_machine: Within new_playbook, STEP advances local s.sp and nesting_depth, while ENDSTEP decrements both; an empty line terminates parsing. Playbook allocation state is global, whereas s.sp is local to each invocation.
